- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.3), model often underestimates; raise forecast by 5–10% to avoid missing downward momentum.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward spikes; apply a 1–2 day lag correction by reducing forecast by 3–5% on next day.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; apply mean reversion bias: subtract 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates early in the horizon; cap first 5–7 days at 1–2% below historical 30d mean.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.5–0.75 range, model tends to drift; apply smoothing filter: average last 3 sentiment values to adjust forecast slope.
